extracted.intended_audience: EPA Assistant Administrators, EPA rulemaking staff, and agency decisionmakers (with relevance to stakeholders and advocacy groups)
extracted.subtask_short: request public hearings and comment extension
extracted.subtask_description: A formal advocacy letter asking EPA to hold in-person public hearings and to provide 120-day comment periods for two specific proposed rules (CCR Part A closure deadlines and revised ELG for steam electric power plants). The letter explains why in-person hearings and longer comment periods are legally and practically necessary and requests a prompt agency response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for in-person public hearing for each proposed rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The 87 undersigned groups ... ask EPA to hold an in-person public hearing on each proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale and supporting points: "A genuine public hearing serves many critical functions. It offers any member of the public the opportunity to speak directly to agency representatives, who are physically present in the room." The letter emphasizes that hearings allow speakers to bring visual aids (maps, photos, contaminated water and soil), have family members or other representatives present as support, and enable the agency and public to see speakers and hear emotional testimony that cannot be conveyed by phone. It asserts that the CCR and ELG proposals are major rulemakings with long-term impacts making in-person hearings appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold hearings in impacted communities (not only in Washington, D.C.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public hearings should be held in communities affected by the rulemaking rather than only in Washington, D.C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporting evidence and precedent: For the CCR rule proposed in 2010, EPA held eight public hearings, including seven in impacted communities outside of the Washington, D.C. area. The letter argues that affected communities must have access to hearings in their local areas so they can participate meaningfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone call-in sessions cannot substitute for in-person hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: "A call session is not an appropriate or legal substitute for in-person public hearings."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation: While call-in opportunities are useful for those unable to attend, they "cannot substitute for an in-person hearing." The letter stresses that phone calls lack the ability to present visual evidence, provide in-person support, and convey the immediacy and emotion of testimony; they also limit the agency's ability to observe speakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide 120-day comment period for each proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Request that EPA provide 120-day comment periods for each proposed rule rather than the announced 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasoning: A 60-day comment period is inadequate because the periods run over Thanksgiving and Christmas, substantially shortening available working days; the two proposals affect many of the same communities and experts, taxing the ability to comment on both simultaneously; and EPA's goal of receiving the best and most comprehensive information is not served by abbreviated periods. "An adequate public comment period will foster robust and informed comment from all stakeholders, and thus result in better rulemaking."

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid scheduling comment periods that run over major holidays
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment periods should not be scheduled so that they run over Thanksgiving and Christmas, which shorten available working days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical impact: Holiday timing reduces the number of working days stakeholders have to prepare substantive comments, particularly when comment periods are already short. The letter cites these holidays as a reason 60 days is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not force simultaneous short comment windows for related proposals affecting the same stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple related proposals involve many of the same impacted communities, public interest groups, experts, and agency or facility staff, the comment process should account for overlapping burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation: The two proposals (CCR Part A and ELG revisions) "involve many of the same impacted communities, public interest groups and experts, thereby severely taxing their ability to comment on both proposals simultaneously." The letter uses this overlap to justify lengthening comment periods or otherwise accommodating stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow statutory mandates and past practice to hold public hearings for major rulemakings
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should adhere to statutory mandates and historical practice to hold public hearings on major rulemakings like these.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal/policy framing: The letter states EPA's failure to hold public hearings is "unprecedented and contrary to law and public policy," and points to EPA's prior conduct (multiple hearings for the 2010 CCR proposal) as precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure the administrative process allows meaningful public input describing harms and proposing protections
rubrics_metrics.description: The public process must enable communities to describe harms from coal ash pollution, voice views on protections, and provide meaningful input into rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanisms: The combination of in-person hearings and extended comment periods is presented as essential to provide the time and forum necessary for impacted individuals and communities to convey harms (e.g., contamination evidence) and recommend protective measures. The letter argues that these steps are "essential to allow the public to describe the harms endured from coal ash pollution, to voice their views on how they can best be protected from toxic waste and to provide meaningful input."

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitate robust public engagement when there is intense public interest and widespread opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is widespread public opposition and intense public interest in a proposal, the agency should facilitate meaningful engagement through hearings and ample comment time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: The letter documents widespread contamination and public concern (citations to reports and statistics) and uses that to justify facilitating engagement. It frames the requested steps as necessary to avoid "deliberately silenc[ing] the voices of Americans nationwide."

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency should provide a timely response and point of contact for the request
rubrics_metrics.description: The letter requests EPA respond by a specified date and provides a contact for follow-up: "We ask that EPA respond to this letter by December 11, 2019 by contacting Lisa Evans at Earthjustice, levans@earthjustice.org, 781-631-4119."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: Requests for hearings and comment extensions should include a clear deadline for agency reply and a named contact to facilitate timely communications and resolution.
